section_summary: This section contains translated Japanese commercial messages intercepted at Chungking, together with three U.S. Embassy cover despatches. The messages concern wartime trade with Indochina and other occupied territories: permits and quotas, barter, rice and other commodities, shipping, insurance, finance, and industrial projects. The section begins and ends within enclosures that continue outside these pages.

subfiles.title: Translations of Japanese commercial messages, October 1943 (continued)
subfiles.from: China Division, Office of War Information
subfiles.about: Commercial intercepts report trading arrangements, permits, shipping, production, and finance across Japan, Indochina, and China.
subfiles.summary: The end of an earlier enclosure contains messages chiefly from October 29–30, 1943. Firms discuss rice bags, lumber, raw silk, hides, rubber barter, rope production, agricultural seed, and credit or remittance problems. Several messages seek urgent permits, shipping space, or approval from company offices and authorities.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1825: Japanese Commercial Messages Intercepted at Chungking
subfiles.from: C. E. Gauss, U.S. Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: The Embassy forwards translations of intercepted Japanese commercial messages from November 1–12.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Office of War Information translations of Japanese commercial messages intercepted November 1–12, 1943.

subfiles.title: Enclosure to Despatch No. 1825: Messages of November 1–12, 1943
subfiles.from: China Division, Office of War Information
subfiles.to: U.S. Embassy, Chungking; Department of State
subfiles.about: The enclosure translates commercial messages intercepted during November 1–12, 1943.
subfiles.summary: The messages document Japanese firms’ efforts to obtain quotas, permits, credit, insurance, and scarce shipping space for trade involving Indochina, China, Japan, and other occupied areas. Repeated subjects include rice and rice bags, timber and sawmills, textiles, hides, pepper, medicines, and industrial equipment. They also describe agricultural projects, freight and warehouse costs, shipping losses, and changing trade controls.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1857: Japanese Commercial Messages Intercepted at Chungking
subfiles.from: C. E. Gauss, U.S. Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: The Embassy forwards translations of intercepted Japanese commercial messages from November 13–18.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Office of War Information translations of messages intercepted November 13–18, 1943.

subfiles.title: Enclosure to Despatch No. 1857: Messages of November 13–18, 1943
subfiles.from: China Division, Office of War Information
subfiles.to: U.S. Embassy, Chungking; Department of State
subfiles.about: The enclosure translates commercial messages intercepted during November 13–18, 1943.
subfiles.summary: These messages cover company qualifications under trade controls, commodity quotas, banking and insurance, and transport and warehouse costs. They include arrangements for cotton, rayon, kapok, sugar, Chinese medicines, opium, machinery, leather, and food production. Several messages address barter with Indochina, delayed shipping, and proposed industrial investments.

subfiles.title: Enclosure to Despatch No. 1874: Messages of November 19–24, 1943 (opening)
subfiles.from: China Division, Office of War Information
subfiles.to: U.S. Embassy, Chungking; Department of State
subfiles.about: The opening page translates November 19 messages on pepper resale, lumber, trade allotments, and pearls.
subfiles.summary: Opening messages concern black-pepper losses, a disputed lumber contract, textile trade allotments, and cultured-pearl orders.
